text:
The air in the precinct was thick with the scent of stale coffee and impending silence, a fitting atmosphere for Detective Howard’s final day. He stood over the desk of his partner, Elias, whose nameplate sat crookedly, a small sign of the chaos that had just erupted. The evidence was undeniable: a ledger, hidden in a false bottom of Elias’s briefcase, detailing bribes taken from the very syndicates they had spent twenty years dismantling.

Howard’s hand trembled as he held the document. The weight of decades of brotherhood pressed against his chest, suffocating him. Elias wasn’t just a partner; he was the brother Howard never had, the man who had pulled him from the wreckage of his first major case, the man who had shared his last bottle of whiskey when his wife left. To report this was to destroy them both. To ignore it was to betray the badge he had worn with pride for thirty years.

As the sun began to set, casting long, blood-orange shadows across the office floor, Howard realized the true nature of his dilemma. It wasn't just about justice; it was about identity. If he turned Elias in, he was no longer Howard the Detective, but Howard the betrayer. If he stayed silent, he was no longer Howard the officer, but Howard the criminal.

He looked at the orange peel on his desk, its vibrant, citrus hue a stark contrast to the gray despair settling in his gut. The color was bright, alive, and deceptive, much like the friendship he was about to sacrifice. He picked up the phone, his finger hovering over the button to call Internal Affairs. The silence in the room was deafening, broken only by the ticking of the clock, each second a hammer blow against his conscience. He had to choose, and in that choice, the man he was would cease to exist.
